title: Centralized Training and Decentralized Control through the Actor-Critic Paradigm for Highly Optimized Multicores
problem: Distributed neural-network-based resource controllers suffer from conflicting control decisions and partial observability, significantly impairing learning and stability of control policies for multicore systems.
motivation: Dynamic voltage frequency scaling on multicores requires robust control that handles partial observability and coordinated resource allocation across cores, a challenge conventional distributed controllers fail to address.
method: A central neural network (the "critic") monitors the overall system and evaluates performance under temperature constraints. Separate neural networks on each processor core (the "actors") independently choose DVFS actions—that is, how to adjust each core's speed and power consumption. All these networks learn together through actor-critic reinforcement learning, where the critic scores the actors' decisions and the actors improve based on that feedback. This centralized training resolves two problems: cores no longer make conflicting DVFS decisions, and each core gets better visibility into the full system state.
key_novelty: Using centralized training with decentralized actors for multicore DVFS control, so individual cores coordinate their speed-and-power decisions instead of conflicting.
contributions: Novel actor-critic reinforcement learning framework for multicore DVFS control
Centralized critic providing system-wide context to decentralized actors
Average 20% and peak 34% performance improvements over state-of-the-art on real-world platform
Improved stability of control policies under temperature constraints
limitations: Not discussed; evaluation limited to DVFS without broader system-level integration.
